walkthroughs.h2: What counts as a mental health problem?
walkthroughs.body_html: Psychologists use criteria such as statistical infrequency, deviation from social norms, failure to function and deviation from ideal mental health. No single definition is perfect, so clinicians use the DSM or ICD to diagnose.

To be diagnosed, a person typically has five or more symptoms for at least two weeks, including low mood or loss of pleasure. Other symptoms: sleep changes, fatigue, guilt, poor concentration. Severity can be mild, moderate or severe.
Addiction has three core features: tolerance (needing more), withdrawal (symptoms when stopping) and compulsion. It can be to a substance like nicotine or to a behaviour like gambling.
